$comment: AUTHORED, like pricing.json, and the one act-6 data file that is not a count. Every field below is transcribed from a decision record or its plan - the reference is on the field. Do not add a field that has no `from`.
_source: CurriculumWebsite/docs/decisions/0004-two-track-delivery.md (accepted 2026-07-26) for the two tracks, their names and their bands; docs/curriculum/two-track-differentiation-plan.md §1.2 for the axes; ChessCurriculumProject/curriculum/pathways.json for the Stage-1 compression figure Challenger cites.
label: the same sessions, two ways to run them
aside: set per group · a coach can override per child
asideFrom: two-track-differentiation-plan.md §5: 'Track choice is a per-group setting the academy makes; coaches can override per child (age ≠ level — a strong 7-year-old can run Challenger).'

explorer.name: Explorer
explorer.positions: Foundation and Core are the set, Challenge is the coach's to show
explorer.from: ADR-0004 (≈5–7; shorter segments, more guided practice and mini-games, fewer but higher-quality puzzles, slower abstraction); plan §1.2 (5–8 min blocks, more transitions; subset of 4–5 of the 8, the Foundation/Core tier; mini-games first, full games later)
explorer.short: 5–8 minute blocks · Foundation and Core are the set

challenger.name: Challenger
challenger.positions: all eight, with the Challenge tier the point of the hour
challenger.from: ADR-0004 (≈8–12; faster pacing, merged introductory concepts, earlier notation/coordinates, harder puzzles, earlier practical games); plan §1.2 (10–15 min blocks; all 8, Challenge tier emphasized; full games early; notation introduced early)
challenger.short: 10–15 minute blocks · all eight, Challenge the point

shared: Both tracks reach the same educational outcomes; the difference is HOW, not WHAT.
shortNote: The one-line form the shortest phones print instead of the full readout, so no window loses a clause mid-sentence. Same device as pricing.json's `addsShort`.
